focus: 'is being' /ɪzbiːɪŋ/ · 'has been' in passives · 'have something done' (causative) stress · 'get it done' · agent-less passive rhythm across tenses
focus_ar: 'is being' و'has been' في المبني للمجهول، ونبر 'have something done'، و'get it done'، وإيقاع المجهول بدون فاعل في كل الأزمنة
arabic_challenge: B2 passives stack two or three weak auxiliaries ('it's being repaired', 'it had been sold'), and the causative 'have something done' puts the stress on the PARTICIPLE at the end, not the object. Arabic learners over-stress the auxiliaries and mis-stress the causative, which then sounds like a normal perfect tense.

isolation.instructions: 'is being' compresses to /ɪzbiːɪŋ/ — two weak auxiliaries in a row — then the participle is stressed: 'the road's being REPAIRED'. Don't stress either auxiliary.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'is being' تُدمج إلى /ɪzbiːɪŋ/ — مساعدان خفيفان — ثم التصريف الثالث منبور: 'the road's being REPAIRED'.

sentence_practice: The road is being repaired at the moment.
New flats are being built near us.
daily_drills.record_this: The main road is being repaired at the moment, so traffic is terrible. New flats are being built right next to our building. The whole matter is being investigated by an independent team.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'the road is being repaired'. Are both 'is' and 'being' weak, with 'rePAIRED' stressed?

isolation.instructions: Perfect passives stack 'has/had' + 'been': 'it's been SOLD' /ɪtsbɪn/, 'it had been SOLD' /ɪtədbɪn/. All auxiliaries stay weak; only the participle is strong.
isolation.instructions_ar: المجهول التام يجمع has/had + been: 'it's been SOLD'. كل المساعدات خفيفة والتصريف قوي.

sentence_practice: The house has been sold already.
All the emails have been sent.
The building had been abandoned for years.
daily_drills.record_this: The house has already been sold to a young family. All the emails have been sent out this morning. The old building had been abandoned for years before they restored it.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'it's been sold'. Do 's and 'been' both stay weak, with 'SOLD' carrying the stress?

target_sounds: causative 'have something done' — stress the participle

isolation.instructions: 'I had my hair CUT' means someone else did it for me. Critically, the stress goes on the FINAL participle, not on 'hair'. Compare: 'I had my hair CUT' (service) vs 'I CUT my hair' (myself).
isolation.instructions_ar: 'I had my hair CUT' معناها شخص آخر فعلها لي، والنبر على التصريف الأخير لا على 'hair'.

sentence_practice: I had my hair cut yesterday.
She had her eyes tested last week.
daily_drills.record_this: I had my hair cut yesterday afternoon at the new place. We're having the whole kitchen painted next month. She had her eyes tested last week and needs new glasses.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I had my hair cut'. Is the stress on 'CUT' at the end, making it clearly a service?

isolation.instructions: 'get' replaces 'have' in informal speech, with the same stress pattern: 'I need to get my car FIXED', 'let's get it DONE'. It often adds a sense of effort or urgency.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'get' تحلّ محل 'have' في الكلام غير الرسمي بنفس النبر: 'get my car FIXED'، وتضيف إحساس الجهد أو الاستعجال.

sentence_practice: I need to get my car fixed.
daily_drills.record_this: I really need to get my car fixed before the weekend. Let's just get it done today and stop delaying. You should definitely get that cough checked by a doctor.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'get my car fixed'. Is the stress on 'FIXED' at the end?

target_sounds: agent-less passive rhythm in formal description

isolation.instructions: Formal English uses agent-less passives to sound objective: 'It has been decided', 'Applications will be reviewed'. Keep the auxiliary chain flat and light, then land firmly on the participle.
isolation.instructions_ar: الإنجليزية الرسمية تستخدم المجهول بدون فاعل ليبدو موضوعيًا. اجعل سلسلة المساعدات مسطحة وخفيفة والتصريف قويًا.

sentence_practice: It has been decided that the office will close.
Applications will be reviewed next week.
All forms must be completed in ink.
daily_drills.record_this: It has been decided that the office will close for renovation. All applications will be reviewed carefully next week. Every form must be completed in ink and signed at the bottom.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'it has been decided'. Is the auxiliary chain flat and light, landing firmly on 'deCIDed'?

challenge_sentences: The road is being repaired at the moment.
The house has already been sold.
I had my hair cut yesterday.
It has been decided that the office will close.
daily_drills.record_this: The main road is being repaired at the moment. The house has already been sold to a young couple. I had my hair cut yesterday at the new salon. It has been decided that the office will close for two weeks.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: weak auxiliary chains, 'being' vs 'been', and stress on the final participle in causatives.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself describing renovations to a building, mixing passive tenses with causatives. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تصف ترميم مبنى، ممزوجًا بين أزمنة المجهول والصيغة السببية، وبعدين اسمع وراجع.
test_yourself.passage: Our building is finally being renovated after years of complaints. The roof had been leaking since long before we moved in, and nothing had ever been repaired properly. Last month it was announced that the work would begin in March. So far, the windows have been replaced and the stairwell has been repainted. At the moment the lift is being modernised, which means we're all walking up five floors. Each flat is being inspected individually, and we've been told to report any damage. I've already had my kitchen tap replaced and I'm getting the bathroom tiles redone next week. My neighbour had her whole flat rewired last year, so she's relaxed about it. It's been estimated that everything will be finished by autumn, though I suspect it'll be delayed.

sounds_to_check.'is being' + participle: is being renovated, is being modernised, is being inspected
sounds_to_check.perfect passives: had been leaking, had been repaired, have been replaced, has been repainted, we've been told, it's been estimated
sounds_to_check.causative 'have/get something done': had my kitchen tap rePLACED, getting the bathroom tiles reDONE, had her whole flat reWIRED
sounds_to_check.modal passives: would begin, will be finished, it'll be delayed

scoring_guide.90_100: Flat weak auxiliary chains, clear being/been, correct causative stress. Ready for week 10.
scoring_guide.50_69: Causative stress on the object, or being/been confused. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, keeping auxiliaries weak and stressing the final participle.

for_arabic_speakers: Passives stack weak auxiliaries — keep the whole chain light and land firmly on the participle only.
'being' /biːɪŋ/ = in progress; 'been' /bɪn/ = completed. Never swap them.
The causative 'have/get something DONE' stresses the FINAL participle — that is what marks it as a service someone did for you.
'get something done' is the informal version of 'have something done', often with a sense of urgency.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
